full_judgment:
2. This application has been filed under section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908, by the defendants-appellants-petitioners, Assistant Commissioner (Land), Mirzapur, Tangail and others, for condonation of delay of 5415 days occurred in filing this revisional application placed with this Rule. 

 6. Being aggrieved thereby, the defendants-respondents have filed this application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure along with an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908, seeking condonation of delay of 5415 days in filing this revisional application, whereupon the instant Rule has been issued. 

 8. Learned Advocate Mr Shishir Kanti Mazumder appeared for the opposite parties. Having placed the paragraph No. 4 of the Counter Affidavit, he submits that, the Government's pleader has contested in the appeal and argued before the appellate court and was aware of the judgment passed in the appeal and in his presence. Hence, admittedly, the defendant-respondent was aware of the judgment and decree passed in the appeal, but they did not challenge the same knowing fully well, because they had no interest. He also submits that, the contention that they could not file this revisional application due to misplacement of the record is absolutely false and ex-facie untrue. He then submits that, the petitioners were aware of the judgment of the appeal as a contesting party, but they could not give any explanation at all, for less than sufficient or satisfactory, about the reason for delay of more than 8 years and this cannot be condoned in the light of the decision reported in 2001 BLD (AD) 35 = 6 BLC (AD) /01: between Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, Ministry of Works and others vs Mr Alauddin. He points out that, in the case reported in 2001 BLD (AD) 35 = 6 BLC (AD) 101, the Apex Court has considered the sluggishness in the movement of the Government authorities and, even, by giving them the highest degree of leeway the Apex Court has refused to condone a delay of 1340 days, whereas it is the case of 5,415 days of abnormal and unexplained delay. The learned Advocate, with reference to the statement made in paragraph No.2 of the application and the statutory provisions of section 5 of the Limitation Act, submits that, no such explanation, as contemplated in section 5, has been given in paragraph Nos. 2 and 3 about the delay of 5415 days. The learned Advocate asserts that, the sole consideration for disposal of this application is to see as to whether the petitioner has been able to make out a case of "sufficient explanation" as required by section 5 of the Act, which the petitioners has failed to do in this case. He emphatically argues that, this application cannot be disposed of upon consideration of any extraneous ground whatsoever. He concludes that, this is a fit case, where the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 11. The provisions of section 5 of the Limitation Act reads as follows:- 

 5. Extension of period in certain cases—Any appeal or application for a revision or a review of judgment or for leave to appeal or any other application to which this may he made applicable by or under any enactment for the time being in force may be admitted after the period of limitation prescribed thereof, when the applicant or applicant satisfies the Court that he had sufficient cause for not preferring the appeal or making the application within such period. 

 Explanation—The fact that the applicant or applicant was misled by any order, practice or judgment of the High Court Division in ascertaining or computing the prescribed period of limitation may be sufficient cause within the meaning of this section. 

 13. Now, the question is as to whether in the light of the provisions of section 5 of the Act, the petitioner has been able to prove or show that there was sufficient cause for not preferring this revisional application within stipulated period of limitation.
